newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu loyalists move to oust new Zaire premier.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu loyalists move to oust new Zaire premier.

text.p: Allies of Zaire's beleaguered President Mobutu Sese Seko began moves on Friday to oust opposition stalwart Etienne Tshisekedi for excluding them from power in his first act since becoming prime minister.

The political confusion in Kinshasa further complicated efforts to convene peace talks in South Africa this weekend between representatives of Mobuto and rebels who have captured a quarter of Zaire in a drive to unseat him.
The Zaire government's negotiators were already in South Africa, discussing arrangements for the talks, originally due to start on Saturday. But there was no confirmation the rebel side had arrived.
Diplomatic sources said Tshisekedi's appointment, and the ensuing controversy, had complicated the situation. The rebels have shown open contempt for politicians who served Mobutu's 31-year rule.
Mobutu himself refused to be drawn into the political crisis stirred by Tshisekedi, telling reporters on Friday this was not the business of the head of state.

Tshisekedi made enemies even among his supporters in parliament on Thursday by dissolving the transitional assembly, dominated by Mobuto supporters. Leaders of the pro-Mobutu FPC parliamentary majority called urgent talks on Friday with the pro-Tshisekedi members to agree strategy on ousting him.

At the same time Tshisekedi unveiled a 26-member government excluding Mobutu's associates but with six key portfolios reserved for Laurent Kabila's rebels. The rebels, who insist Mobutu must go, rejected the offer.

"We have not ousted Tshisekedi. He has ousted himself," FPC vice-president Mutombo Bakafu Asenda told Reuters. "We do not recognise that there is a prime minister...we cannot apply the rules of the constitution to maintain a prime minister who does not himself recognise the constitution."
Mutombo said Friday's meetings with the opposition alliance would discuss a new prime minister. Tshisekedi said he was forming a government by decree without submitting it to lawmakers.
Tshisekedi was nominated by parliament on Tuesday, nearly two weeks after the assembly voted out prime minister Kengo wa Dondo, accused of mismanaging the government's war effort.
Mobutu on Friday distanced himself from the appointment of Tshisekedi or the turmoil it kicked off.

"It is not a matter that concerns the head of state," Mobutu said as he and Tshisekedi went into talks on Friday. "It is the political class that agreed on a name proposed by the opposition because the prime minister has to come from the political camp other than that of the head of state's."
Tshisekedi emerged two hours later, saying he briefed Mobutu on his decisions: "I confirmed what I said yesterday."
In the eastern Zairean city of Goma, captured by rebels early in their offensive, a spokesman dismissed the offer of six ministerial posts in Zaire's new government as a joke.

Gaten Kakudji, secretary-general of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, told Reuters rebels were not interested in such cabinet posts. He said the rebel aim was to topple Mobutu and his government.

"Tshisekedi's offer is little more than comedy to amuse the gallery and people of Kinshasa but it lacks all logic. He is Mobutu's prime minister and he knows our objectives but he still offers us places in Mobutu's government," Kakudji said. "Our mission is radical change in this country."
